assign.outcome:
**The site is off opaque button fills.** 101 invisible pairs / 504 elements -> **19 / 50**, same 76 pages, same bar. Not one of the 50 is a control you cannot see.

![the demo toolbar, before](toolbar-before-1920.png)
![and after](toolbar-after-1920.png)

**What moved.** The `--shade / --paper / --fill-aNN` ladder now lives in `framework.css` `:root`, documented rung by rung; the [lab](/framework/styles/stacks/) redeclares nothing and became the regression test. `.btn, button` and inline `code` take `--fill-a08`, `th` takes `--fill-a04`, and `.demo-btn` + `.layout-btn` stop painting nothing at all. lew42's `border: none` on buttons is **deleted** - at (0,2,0) it had been cancelling framework.css's hairline AND every component's `border-color` on `:hover`, so a hover border was setting the colour of a border whose style was none. 21 files; the fence allowed 32.

**One regression the scan could not see, caught by eye.** With an alpha fill, a default button on a `prim` or `dark` section band went to near-black ink on a DARKENED orange - 3.4:1, where the opaque white fill had been 10:1. Fixed in `styles/sections/tone.js`: a coloured band declares `color-scheme: dark`, and the `dark` tone paints `--bg` instead of `--ink`. An island that INVERTS with the mode cannot declare a fixed scheme, because the same line flips its own background - so the fix is to paint it from a floor that stays dark, and then declare it. That also hands the band `--wash` and `--tint` in the right direction, which is the background twin of `.muted` that `layouts/home/page.js` says it never had.

![section bands, dark mode](bands-after-1920-dark.png)

**The matrix, both modes** - failing cells 14 -> 9 light, 13 -> 9 dark, measured as an A/B on the same build with the four changed declarations put back at document-start. The nine survivors are the same nine in both modes: seven placement cells and two compression cells, all of them arguments the page is making on purpose.

![the matrix cells, light](matrix-cells-light.png)

**Deliberately left.**

- `button.prim` on `--prim` and `button.bg` on `--bg` stay opaque. An accent can only be invisible on one floor, its own, so it is a **placement** error and the fix is to move the button - now rule 6 of [stacking.md](/framework/styles/doc/stacking.md). Neither occurs outside the matrix cell built to show it.
- Eight fills that must OCCLUDE live content stay opaque - a floating pill, a label over a ruler, a chip over a canvas, a segment that is a card in its own right. A floor is a floor whatever it is shaped like; all eight are named in the doc.
- Transparent icon buttons keep their transparent rest state - 25 of the surviving 50. Their hover and `.on` fills went alpha, so the states you have to read now work on any floor. Whether an icon button should carry a RESTING fill is a design question, not a measurement one, and it is yours.
- 13 more are the scan's own class-name test reading a text label as a chip (`.layout-tag` has no fill and never wanted one). Tightening it in the same wave that changed the site would have made before and after incomparable.

Zero console errors on a 20-url sweep; 11 pages shot at 1920 in light and dark, nothing looks worse by eye.
